- The introduction of these parameters is well-intentioned but requires careful handling to ensure that they do not lead to incorrect or unexpected behavior.

Consider adding more deterministic test cases to complement the existing ones.

The addition of `assertShardFailures` method in `BaseEqlSpecTestCase.java` is a good step towards ensuring that shard failures are properly handled and tested. The changes in `asArray` and `BaseEqlSpecTestCase` constructors are necessary to accommodate the new parameters. Ensure that these changes do not break existing test cases and that all relevant constructors are updated consistently.
The introduction of `EqlSpecFailingShardsTestCase.java` and `EqlSpecFailingShardsIT.java` is a good way to isolate tests related to shard failures. Ensure that these new test cases cover all necessary scenarios and do not overlap with existing ones unnecessarily.

review_comment:
`allowPartialResultsInBody` value seems to suggest that "partial results" settings can be used **either** as request parameter or request body parameter. I think we should test the case when the user provides:
- request parameter values AND request body parameters (both of them or just one)
- either one of them

In other words, randomize any combination of request parameters presence and values in the two places where we allow them.

review_comment: What happens if an user provides only `allow_partial_sequece_results=true` or uses `allow_partial_search_results=false` and `allow_partial_sequece_results=true` at the same time?

`allow_partial_sequece_results` alone (or with  `allow_partial_search_results=false`) has no effect.
There are randomized tests for this in [PartialSearchResultsIT](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/116388/files#diff-394483381f9a9290704dec509e32ba564499cf341a3b0ee536f7463537137aebR210) , but probably I can extend them a bit, randomly setting `allow_partial_search_results=false`

review_comment: It would be great if all the existent tests in EQL that have no idea about partial results (all the tests based on BaseEqlSpecTestCase before this PR) would completely randomize these two new settings. All of them should behave completely the same because we have no "broken" shard setup for them which means that irrespective of the values provided, the tests should pass.
There is some randomization already, but I'm making it more complete.
